subject: Short-term SLA uplift request — Black Friday pilot (HeliosCommerce)
messages:
From: Emily Helms <emily.helms@helioscommerce.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement_ops@helioscommerce.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Request: temporary rate-band elevation for Black Friday pilot

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the intro call last week. Quick ask: we’re running a two-day Black Friday pilot (Oct 22–23, high-visibility traffic spike) for our checkout personalization models and expect a short window of sustained high QPS that will overflow the current fair-share bucket.

Estimated surge:~
- Peak sustained qps: 180 req/s (endpoints using generation with ~500 tokens avg)
- Anticipated total tokens (pilot window): ~120M tokens over 48 hours

Can Redwood provide a short-term elevated rate band or dedicated priority token pool for a 48-hour window to avoid repeated throttling? We’re flexible on a capped extra spend; need confirmation on:

1) Whether a temporary priority allocation is supported (and how it interacts with fairness policies)
2) Expected latency SLO under the uplift (p95 / p99 targets)
3) Required contract/PO or DocuSign addendum to authorize the exception

Attaching our forecast and a small traffic sample for context. If you can propose an approach and rough cost estimate by EOD Wed we can move fast — this is time-sensitive.

Best,
Emily Helms
Head of Ops, HeliosCommerce
[Attachment: helios_bf_forecast.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Helms <emily.helms@helioscommerce.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-band elevation for Black Friday pilot

Emily —

Thanks for the forecast, this is exactly the kind of heads-up that helps. Short answer: yes, we can support a short-term elevated allocation. I’m looping in Laura (your AE) for commercial and Rishi from Reliability to scope the technical config.

A few quick clarifying Qs so we can size the pool:
- Is 180 req/s peak sustained across a single route/model or split across multiple endpoints?
- Are requests latency-sensitive (i.e., do you need <250ms p95)?
- Do you have DR/backup routing preference if we hit capacity limits?

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi to propose a token-pool + fair-share carveout config and a fallback plan.
2) Laura to prepare a short SLA addendum + pricing for the 48-hour window.
3) We’ll provide a DocuSign addendum you can sign; once countersigned we’ll enable the priority pool.

Looping in both now — expect a technical proposal by tomorrow EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Internal note: attaching initial checklist]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Helms <emily.helms@helioscommerce.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-band elevation for Black Friday pilot

Emily —

Happy to handle the commercial side. We can grant a temporary priority token pool for the Oct 22–23 window with the following guardrails:

- Fixed token pool: 150M tokens for the 48-hour window (billed in advance at a negotiated uplift)
- Latency target during pool use: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms (region: us-east-1)
- Fairness policy: priority pool consumes dedicated capacity before fair-share; if exhausted requests will fall back to standard fair-share throttling.
- Contract: one-page SLA addendum + email PO accepted. I’ll draft the addendum and send a DocuSign link — expected close in 24 hours from acceptance.

Pricing option A: pre-purchase token pool at 1.4x standard token rate (recommended for predictable cost)
Pricing option B: on-demand overage at 2.2x standard rate (higher variance)

I’ve attached a draft addendum; Ben/Rishi — please confirm the technical config so I can finalize pricing.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sla_addendum_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Emily Helms <emily.helms@helioscommerce.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-band elevation for Black Friday pilot

Thanks Laura — that framework looks workable. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

- We can commit to the 150M token pre-purchase if you include an unused-token credit back at 70% of the purchase price for any tokens not consumed during the window.
- Latency: our internal SLA requires p95 <= 250ms for checkout scoring. Would Redwood be able to meet p95=250ms or is 300ms the realistic floor during heavy contention?
- Fallback behavior: please confirm what happens to in-flight requests when the priority pool is exhausted — will they be queued, rejected with 429, or routed to a lower-cost model automatically?
- Observability: can you create a temporary read-only Console link for our infra team during the window (token-level usage + queueing metrics)?

Attaching a sample traffic trace and a quick note from our infra leads. We’re aiming to finalize procurement by Wed EOD so appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emily
[Attachment: bf_traffic_sample.json (application/json)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Helms <emily.helms@helioscommerce.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-band elevation for Black Friday pilot — proposed final steps

Emily —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Finalizing scope below so procurement can sign off:

Technical (Rishi):
- Priority token pool: 150M tokens, enabled Oct 22 00:00 to Oct 23 23:59 (US/Eastern).
- Latency SLO while using priority pool: p95 <= 250ms (we’ll run an autoscaling buffer and enable optimized kernels for the period).
- Fallback: when the pool is exhausted requests will be returned 429 by default; we can optionally enable automatic model-fallback (to a smaller/cheaper variant) if you want degraded-but-successful responses — confirm preference.
- Observability: temporary read-only Console access (token-level telemetry + queue depth + p95/p99) will be provisioned for your infra emails.

Commercial (Laura):
- Pricing: pre-purchase option accepted at 1.4x standard token rate with unused-token credit at 70% refund credit — we’ll reflect this in the addendum.
- Sign-off path: Laura will send DocuSign addendum; procurement to countersign and we’ll enable the pool within 2 hours of counter-signature.

Next actions:
1) Laura to send DocuSign addendum (today).
2) Emily confirm whether you want automatic model-fallback or strict 429 reject behavior.
3) On countersignature we’ll schedule a short runbook sync with Rishi + your infra.

If that all looks good I’ll mark the deal HLX-5792 as scoped and we’ll issue the addendum link.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — ben@redwoodinference.com
